q: 1. The free board in a channel is governed by the
explain: Freeboard is the safety margin between the full supply level and the top of the bank to prevent overtopping.

q: 2. The saturation gradient in an ordinary loam soils is, usually, kept from
explain: The saturation line (phreatic line) in loam soil banks is typically assumed to have a slope of 4:1 for design stability.

q: 3. The height of dowel above the road level should not be more than
explain: A dowel is a small curb on the canal bank road to prevent vehicles from falling; 30 cm is the standard maximum height.

q: 4. The width of dowel is, usually, kept from
explain: Dowels typically range from 0.3 to 0.6 meters in width to remain stable and functional as a safety curb.

q: 5. A spoil bank is formed when the
options: volume of excavation is in excess of the embankment filling
explain: When the earth excavated from the canal is more than what is needed for the banks, the surplus is piled into 'spoil banks'.

q: 6. The borrow pits should, preferably, be taken from
options: the field on the right side of canal
the field on the left side of the canal
the central half width of the section of the canal
explain: Taking borrow pits from the canal bed (central width) is preferred because they will eventually fill with silt, making the canal bed smoother.

q: 7. In case of small channels, the borrow pits should start from a distance not less than ............. from the toe of the embankment.
explain: A safe distance (minimum 5m) is maintained to prevent the borrow pit from undermining the stability of the canal embankment.

q: 8. When the quantity of the earth is much in excess of the quantity required for filling, it has to be deposited in the form of spoil banks. The spoil banks are made on
explain: Depending on available land and the volume of excess soil, spoil banks can be constructed on either or both sides of the canal alignment.

q: 9. Lining of a canal is necessary
options: to minimize the seepage losses in canal
to prevent erosion of bed and sides due to high velocities
to increase the discharge in canal section by increasing the velocity
explain: Lining creates a smooth, impermeable surface that saves water, allows for higher non-erodible velocities, and improves discharge capacity.

q: 10. Lining of canal ............. the maintenance of the canal.
explain: Lining prevents weed growth and silting, which significantly reduces the frequency and cost of annual maintenance.

q: 11. Lining of a canal
options: increases available head for power generation
explain: A lined canal is more stable, loses less water to seepage, and maintains a steeper energy gradient useful for small-scale hydro projects.

q: 12. The sodium carbonate lining consists of at least
explain: A low-cost lining method involves mixing approximately 1% sodium carbonate with 6% clay into the soil to reduce permeability.

q: 13. For the repairing of an old but sound concrete lining, the lining preferred is
explain: Shotcrete (pneumatically applied mortar) is ideal for repairing cracks or resurfacing existing concrete structures.

q: 14. The weed growth in a canal leads to
explain: Weeds increase the rugosity (roughness) of the channel, which slows down the water velocity and reduces the overall discharge capacity.

q: 15. Kennedy, in his silt theory, assumed that the silt is kept in suspension because of eddies generated from the
explain: Kennedy's theory simplified the mechanics by assuming only the vertical eddies rising from the canal bed support the silt particles.

q: 16. Kennedy gave a relation between
options: critical velocity and the depth of flowing water
explain: Kennedy's fundamental equation ($V_0 = 0.55D^{0.64}$) relates the critical velocity (no silting, no scouring) to the depth of water ($D$).

q: 17. The relation given by Kennedy for critical velocity in m/s is
explain: This is the standard formula where 'm' is the critical velocity ratio and 'D' is the depth.

q: 18. A channel is said to be in scouring when the critical velocity ratio is ............. one.
explain: If the CVR ($m$) is greater than 1, the actual velocity is higher than the critical velocity required to prevent scouring, leading to bed erosion.

q: 19. According to Kennedy, the silt transporting power of a channel is proportional to
explain: Kennedy derived that the silt carrying capacity of a channel varies with the 2.5 (or 5/2) power of its velocity.

q: 20. According to Lacey, a channel is said to be in regime, if
options: it flows in incoherent unlimited alluvium of the same character as that transported material
the silt grade and the silt charge are constant
explain: Lacey's 'True Regime' conditions require constant discharge, constant silt properties, and flow through an unlimited alluvial bed.

q: 21. The main cause of silting in channel is
explain: Silting occurs when velocity drops (due to poor slope or design) or when excessive silt enters through the head regulator.

q: 22. According to Lacey
options: the silt is kept in suspension due to the force of vertical eddies
the eddies are generated from bed and sides, both normal to the surface of generation
the vertical component of eddies generated from sides will also support the silt
explain: Unlike Kennedy, Lacey accounted for eddies generated from the entire wetted perimeter (bed and sides).

q: 23. Lacey assumed that silt is kept in suspension because of the normal components of eddies generated from the
explain: Lacey's theory improved upon Kennedy's by stating that eddies arise from the whole perimeter, including the sides.

q: 24. Lacey gave a relation between
explain: Lacey provided a comprehensive set of equations relating $V$, $R$, $A$, $Q$, and $S$ for regime channels.

q: 25. The channel after attaining its section and longitudinal slope, will be said to be in ............. regime.
explain: Final regime is the state reached when a channel has adjusted its perimeter, depth, and slope to become stable in alluvium.

q: 26. The general regime flow equation is
explain: This is Lacey's general flow equation derived for regime channels in alluvium.

q: 27. If m is the mean particle diameter of the silt in mm, the Lacey's silt factor (f) is given by
explain: The silt factor $f$ determines the roughness and required velocity of the channel based on the bed material size.

q: 28. Distributary head regulators are provided
options: to control the supplies to the off-taking channel
to control the silt entry in the off-taking canal
to stop the supply, when not needed, in the off-taking canal
explain: These regulators act as valves to manage discharge, sediment intake, and closure for the smaller off-taking canal.

q: 29. Cross regulators are provided
options: to raise the water level to its upstream during the periods of low discharges in the parent channel
to help in closing the supply to downstream of the parent channel
to absorb fluctuation in various sections of the canal system
explain: Cross regulators are built across the main canal to back up water for off-takes and control flow downstream.

q: 30. A structure constructed in an irrigation canal for the purpose of wasting some of its water, is known as a
explain: Escapes act as safety valves to discharge excess water caused by heavy rain or sudden closures of off-takes.

q: 31. Escapes are also known as ............. for the canals.
explain: They protect the canal banks from overtopping and breaching during emergency conditions.

q: 32. The capacity of escape channel should not be less than ............. of the capacity of the parent channel at that point.
explain: To be effective as an emergency safety structure, an escape must be able to handle at least 50% of the canal's design discharge.

q: 33. A fall, which maintains the depth is a
explain: A trapezoidal notch fall is designed so that the depth-discharge relationship of the fall matches the canal itself, maintaining constant depth.

q: 34. The Sarda canal has a
explain: The Sarda type fall is a classic example of a vertical drop fall, used when the discharge is small and the drop is around 1 to 1.5 meters.

q: 35. In Sarda type fall, the length of the crest is kept ............. the bed width of the canal.
explain: Standard design for a Sarda fall keeps the crest length equal to the bed width of the incoming canal.

q: 36. In a Sarda type fall, the width of the trapezoidal crest (B) is given by
explain: This empirical formula is used to calculate the stable top width of the crest for a trapezoidal Sarda fall.

q: 37. The relation for discharge (Q) over a rectangular crest of a Sarda fall is
explain: This is the modified weir formula used for the rectangular crest design of a Sarda type fall.

q: 38. A baffle wall is a sort of low weir constructed at the end of the cistern to
options: head up water to its upstream to such a high that hydraulic jump is formed
withstand the actual impact of the high velocity jet to dissipate the energy
explain: The baffle wall (or baffle platform) helps ensure the hydraulic jump occurs within the paved cistern to protect the bed.

q: 39. A parabolic glacis type fall is commonly known as
explain: The Montague fall utilizes a parabolic glacis to efficiently guide water into the cistern and promote energy dissipation.

q: 40. When the water is thrown into a well over a crest from where it escapes near its bottom, the type of fall is called
explain: A cylinder fall (well fall) uses a vertical shaft to drop water, making it suitable for very large drops and small discharges.

q: 41. A sudden fall of level of ground along the alignment of a canal joined by an inclined bed is called a
explain: Rapid falls consist of a long sloping glacis and are used where the natural ground slope is steeper than the canal bed slope.

q: 42. The cylinder or well fall is quite suitable and economical for
explain: Well falls are ideal for dropping small amounts of water over high vertical distances, such as in hilly terrain.

q: 43. The discharge (Q) over trapezoidal crest of Sarda fall is ............. as compared to rectangular crest of identical parameters.
explain: Due to the wider side area in a trapezoidal shape, the discharge capacity is slightly higher than a rectangular crest of the same base width.

q: 44. The Ingles type fall makes use of ............. impact for energy dissipation.
explain: The Ingles (or baffle) fall uses a vertical impact of the water jet against a baffle wall to dissipate kinetic energy.

q: 45. The fall which can be used as meter fall, is
explain: A flumed glacis fall can be calibrated to accurately measure the discharge passing through it.

q: 46. A canal outlet should
options: be so designed that the farmer cannot temper with its functioning
be simple so that it can be constructed or fabricated by local masons
draw its fair share of silt carried by the distributing channel
explain: A good outlet (module) must be tamper-proof, simple, and proportional in silt and water distribution.

q: 47. A device which ensures a constant discharge of water passing from one channel to another irrespective of water level in each within certain specified limits, is called
explain: This is the definition of a rigid module, which provides a constant discharge regardless of water level fluctuations.

q: 48. An outlet in which the discharge depends upon the difference in level between the water levels in distributing channel and the water course, is known as
explain: Non-modular outlets (like a simple pipe) vary their discharge based on the water levels of both the parent canal and the field channel.

q: 49. In a flexible outlet, the discharge depends upon the
options: difference of water level between distributary and water course
explain: A semi-module (flexible outlet) depends only on the water level in the parent distributary, not on the field channel level.

q: 50. When discharge of an outlet is independent of the water levels in the water course and the distributary, the outlet is termed as a
explain: A rigid module is designed to provide a fixed flow rate even if water levels change in either channel.
